summary: Connect market, household and service-provider evidence to programme decisions. Explore the five-day course and practical curriculum.
lede: Market systems monitoring for agriculture and rural development programmes connects evidence about prices, traders, households and services to programme decisions. Designed for programme managers, market-systems advisers and MEAL specialists, the course covers actor mapping, results chains and indicator selection, along with data-quality checks and interpretation of evidence about market change and programme contribution for adaptive reviews and reporting.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for development professionals who commission, manage, collect, analyse, or use evidence about agriculture and rural market systems. It suits practitioners with programme or MEAL experience who need to make monitoring findings useful in reviews and adaptive decisions.
prerequisites: Prior experience in agriculture or rural-development programming, market systems work, or monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning is recommended. Basic familiarity with programme indicators and results chains will help you engage with the applied exercises. No coding or programming is required. Spreadsheet familiarity is useful for the monitoring and dashboard exercises.
